You know the swan by now, and the swan knows you.} One kite is stuck in the far hoop, {flapping like a trapped bird|and its first-year is close to tears|and the other kites are jeering at it}. Climb the hoop and free it {You shin up the hoop pole and free the kite. The first-years cheer as if you'd won a race.|You climb, untangle, slide down. The first-year announces your name to the whole field.|You know the hoop pole's footholds by now. The kite goes back to its owner, who tells everyone, loudly.} {You get halfway up the pole and the wind takes your hat and your grip. You land in the long grass, bruised.|The kite comes free and so do you, from rather high up.|You slip on the wet pole and slide down it, slowly and painfully, to applause.} Borrow a kite and fly it {You borrow a fish kite and steer it with a whispered charm. It bites the swan. Everyone is delighted.|You fly a paper dragon in loops until your arms ache with the pull and your face aches with grinning.|You fly your borrowed kite higher than the rest, holding the charm steady against the gusts.}
